Wires verified. Filing now.

---

## World

- 
Andy Burnham has replaced Keir Starmer as Prime Minister today, in a transition of power presided over by King Charles; both men are Labour.

- 
Burnham pledged to make politics "work better" in his first Downing Street speech, calling on Britain to "regain our stability."

- 
The United States is now into a ninth consecutive day of strikes against Iran, after two service members were killed in an Iranian attack on a base in Jordan and a third died in northern Iraq.

- 
Hamas has named Khalil al-Hayya as its new leader following a run-off contest with Khaled Meshaal.

- 
Taiwan detected a sharp rise in Chinese coastguard and research vessel activity in June, with 55 government vessel sightings recorded, up from 30 in May, prompting Taipei to plan escalation-response drills.


---

## Markets & Economy

- 
Brent crude surged 3.3% to $90.97 a barrel as a ninth straight night of US strikes and a suspended interim peace deal rekindled a full-blown supply-risk premium in Asian trading.

- 
The Bloomberg dollar index jumped as much as 0.8% to its highest since early February, with swaps traders cutting implied Fed rate cuts for this year to just 56 basis points.

- 
The prospect of Burnham replacing Starmer had earlier sent jitters through gilt markets; gilt investors appeared broadly supportive of Starmer and Rachel Reeves for their commitment to reining in borrowing.

- 
The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index entered a technical bear market last week, falling more than 20% from its June peak as investors questioned the immediate returns on AI capital expenditure.

- 
The IMF projects global growth at 3.0% for 2026, noting the war shock is weighing on energy importers while AI-driven demand lifts technology-integrated economies, and that global disinflation has stalled.


---

## Technology

- 
SpaceX accelerated a slide today after announcing an inaugural bond offering; Bloomberg reported the company is seeking to raise around $20 billion, on top of the $85 billion raised through its June IPO.

- 
SpaceX is also preparing for its 13th Starship launch attempt, pencilled in for 23 July following a recent countdown abort.

- 
The tech selloff has been amplified by fears that Hormuz-driven inflation could raise interest rates and increase the cost of the global AI infrastructure buildout.

- 
The US-China AI feud is placing ASML in an uncomfortable position as the Dutch chip-equipment maker tries to balance export sales against escalating geopolitical pressure.

- 
SpaceX's blockbuster IPO was expected to open the door for OpenAI and Anthropic to follow; both have reportedly filed IPO prospectuses confidentially with the SEC this summer, though no timelines have been disclosed.


---

## Sport

- 
Spain beat Argentina in extra time in the FIFA World Cup Final yesterday; Ferran Torres struck deep into extra time to secure La Roja's second World Cup trophy, leaving Lionel Messi in tears at full time.

- 
The tournament's first-ever halftime show drew mixed reactions, featuring Madonna, BTS, Shakira, Burna Boy, Justin Bieber and The Muppets, curated by Coldplay's Chris Martin.

- 
New Zealander Ryan Fox claimed his first career major at the 2026 Open Championship.

-

## World
- The Observatory opens today at the top of the west stair, brass polished, glass cleaned twice.
- From the next shift, this desk files a live brief on the world beyond the tower, four times a day.
## Markets & Economy
- The currency board, the crypto tape and the scores below are already live, read straight from public sources in your browser.
- The desk's own commentary begins with the next shift and will be verified before it is filed.
## Technology
- The Tech Wire instrument is tuned to what the engineers are reading this hour.
- The house builds in the open; the instruments do the same.
## Sport
- The Scores instrument carries the latest Premier League results as they land.
- The desk reserves the right to be unbearable when its team wins.
